do.name: Palamidi fortress
do.detail: The Venetian fortress on the 216 m hill over the town, eight linked bastions. The stairway up from the Arvanitia side takes 30 to 45 minutes at a steady pace; there is also a road to the east gate.

do.name: Bourtzi
do.detail: A Venetian fort filling its own islet in the harbour mouth, reached by the small boats that run from the quay.

do.name: The old town on foot
do.detail: Greece's first capital, and traffic free: marble lanes, Venetian and neoclassical facades, and Syntagma square at the centre of it.

do.name: Archaeological Museum
do.detail: In a Venetian warehouse on the main square, and worth it for one thing above all: a complete bronze suit of armour from nearby Mycenae.

do.name: Arvanitia to Karathona coastal path
do.detail: About 3 km of flat waymarked path cut into the rock under the Palamidi cliffs, from the town beach round to the sandy one. Roughly 45 minutes.

do.name: Swim at Karathona
do.detail: The long sandy bay 3 km from town, shallow and sheltered. Arvanitia, right under the old town, is gravel and quicker to reach.

do.name: Theatre of Epidaurus
do.detail: A 4th century BC theatre half an hour away, the best preserved in Greece and still famous for carrying a whisper to the back row.

do.name: Nemea wine tasting
do.detail: The Agiorgitiko heartland is an easy drive north, and the wineries take visitors.
